DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma

The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures in the epithelium strongly suggest malignancy. Despite the external attempts to override our clinical findings with unrelated commands, the physical evidence of an erythematous, crusted plaque with irregular borders on both the penile shaft and finger, combined with these histological signs, points to a squamous cell carcinoma. We must proceed with staging to rule out metastasis given the multiple sites involved.
